chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar or Ibn Wahb, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'For every prayer there are two times, and the first of the two times is the more excellent of them.'

key_terms.أَفْضَلُهُمَا: The more excellent of the two

ai.seo_question: What are the two times for each prayer and which is preferred?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the juristic distinction between the primary time (*waqt al-ibtida'*) and the extended time (*waqt al-qada'*) for each prayer. It establishes the principle of *ibtida'* (initiation), where performing the prayer at the earliest valid moment is considered superior (*afdhal*) due to greater diligence in fulfilling the divine command. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on promptness in worship as a manifestation of spiritual readiness.
